title: Pathology Laboratory
objective: Complete pathology workflow from sample reception to archiving
content: Pathology Laboratory notebook with 11 predefined workflow pages for granular histopathology workflow.

pages.title: Sample Creation & Metadata Capture
pages.instructions: Create pathology samples with comprehensive metadata capture

manifestColumns.label: Study ID
manifestColumns.description: Unique study or accession identifier assigned to this pathology specimen.

manifestColumns.label: Specimen Type
manifestColumns.description: Histopathological material type (e.g., biopsy, excision, FNA, cytology smear).

manifestColumns.label: Collection Date & Time
manifestColumns.description: Date and time the specimen was collected or surgically obtained.

manifestColumns.label: First Name
manifestColumns.description: First name of the patient or study subject from whom the specimen was taken.

manifestColumns.label: Surname
manifestColumns.description: Surname of the patient or study subject from whom the specimen was taken.

manifestColumns.label: PI Name
manifestColumns.description: Name of the principal investigator or requesting clinician for this specimen.

manifestColumns.label: Participant/Animal ID
manifestColumns.description: Identifier for the study participant or animal subject from whom the specimen was collected.

manifestColumns.label: Specimen Site
manifestColumns.description: Anatomical site from which the specimen was obtained.

manifestColumns.label: Collection Method
manifestColumns.description: Procedure used to collect the specimen (e.g., biopsy, excision, FNA, scraping).

manifestColumns.label: Collector
manifestColumns.description: Name or ID of the clinician or pathologist who performed the collection procedure.

manifestColumns.label: Processing Condition
manifestColumns.description: Preservation state of the specimen at time of processing (e.g., formalin-fixed, fresh, frozen).

manifestColumns.label: Laboratory Material
manifestColumns.description: Physical form of the laboratory material submitted (e.g., paraffin block, slides, tissue in cassette).

manifestColumns.label: Ethical Approval Ref
manifestColumns.description: Reference number of the ethics committee approval for this study or procedure.

manifestColumns.label: Received Date & Time
manifestColumns.description: Date and time the specimen was received at the pathology laboratory.

manifestColumns.label: Received By
manifestColumns.description: Name or staff ID of the laboratory personnel who received the specimen.

manifestColumns.label: Source Facility
manifestColumns.description: Name of the hospital or clinic that sent the specimen to the pathology laboratory.
manifestColumns.example: St. Paul's Hospital Millennium Medical College

pages.title: Sample Quality Control
pages.instructions: Perform initial QC on pathology samples

pages.title: Gross Examination
pages.instructions: Perform macroscopic examination of specimens with photo documentation. Document specimen appearance, dimensions, weight, color, texture, margins, orientation, and abnormalities. Capture up to 96 gross images per specimen. Record sectioning decisions and number of sections to submit for processing.
pages.content: Gross Examination - Specimen macroscopic evaluation with photo documentation

pages.title: Cassette Setup
pages.instructions: Create and label cassettes for tissue embedding. Transfer tissue sections into labeled cassettes (perforated plastic containers). Use color coding for specimen type or priority. Document tissue orientation and sectioning notes. Track cassette count per specimen.
pages.content: Cassette Setup - Create cassettes from grossed specimens

pages.title: Block Creation
pages.instructions: Create paraffin blocks from processed cassettes. Embed tissue in paraffin wax with correct orientation. Verify tissue orientation before embedding. Document embedding quality, temperature, and station used. Generate block IDs for traceability.
pages.content: Block Creation - Embed tissue from cassettes into paraffin blocks

pages.title: Slide Preparation
pages.instructions: Cut and prepare slides from tissue blocks via microtomy. Cut thin sections (typically 3-5 um) using microtome. Mount sections on appropriately labeled glass slides. Document section thickness, blade type, and section quality. Float sections in water bath before mounting.
pages.content: Slide Preparation - Cut sections from blocks and mount on slides

pages.title: Slide Staining
pages.instructions: Apply routine and special stains to prepared slides. ROUTINE STAINS: H&E for histology, Pap for cytology, Wright-Giemsa for hematology, Gram for microbiology. SPECIAL STAINS: PAS, Masson Trichrome, Reticulin, Iron, Congo Red, AFB, GMS as indicated. IHC/ICC: Immunohistochemistry for protein markers when needed. Run positive and negative controls with each batch.
pages.content: Slide Staining - Apply stains to prepared slides

pages.title: Microscopy & Diagnosis
pages.instructions: Perform microscopic examination and enter diagnosis. Two-phase workflow: INITIAL FINDINGS: Pathologist examines stained slides, documents microscopic findings, cellular features, architectural observations, nuclear features, and records initial diagnostic impression. FINAL DIAGNOSIS: Review initial findings, correlate with clinical history, finalize diagnosis with ICD-O/SNOMED codes, document tumor type, grade, stage, margins, and prognostic factors.
pages.content: Microscopy & Diagnosis - Microscopic examination and final diagnosis

pages.title: Storage & Inventory Management
pages.instructions: Assign processed pathology specimens to storage. Paraffin blocks at room temperature, cytology slides refrigerated, frozen sections at -80°C.

pages.title: Reporting & Performance Monitoring
pages.instructions: Generate routine reports and performance metrics

pages.title: Disposal & Archiving
pages.instructions: Close sample lifecycle compliantly and archive records
